To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we first report vanadisulfide (VS 2) with high activity in both basal and edges as a co-catalyst for ultrahigh hydrogen production from water splitting.
the vanadium disulfides (VS2) decorated graphitic carbonitride (g C 3 N 4) composite exhibits excellent hydrogen production performance.
vanadium disulfides with high hydrogen evolution activity both in the basal and the edge planes are the cocatalyst of graphitic carbonitrides for ultrahigh photocatalytic hydrogen production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and photocatalytic hydrogen production of vanadium disulfides/graphitic carbon nitrides (VS2/g C3Ns).
the design of a novel vanadium disulfides decorated graphitic carbon nanotubes (g C3 N4) photocatalysts with high solar driven hydrogen evolution activity.
the design and synthesis of novel photocatalysts for solar hydrogen production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work is the first report on vanadium disulfides with high hydrogen evolution activity both in basal plane and edges, which can be used as the cocatalyst of g-C3N4 for ultrahigh hydrogen production.

the VS2/g C 3N4 composite shows a high solar-driven hydrogen generation efficiency, which can be attributed to the synergistic effect of the band structure of VS2 and gC3N4, as well as the high surface area of VS2.

the combination of VS2 and gC3N4 can significantly enhance the hydrogen evolution reaction activity, and the mechanism is related to the high surface activity of VS2 and the band alignment between gC3N and VS2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a new type of photocatalyst for solar hydrogen generation, which is composed of VS2 decorated g-C3N4.
we have successfully prepared VS2/g-C3N4 composite by hydrothermal method and studied its photocatalytic hydrogen production activity.
we have successfully prepared the vanadium disulfides/graphitic carbon nitride composite photocatalyst with ultrahigh solar hydrogen production efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synergistic effect of vanadium disulfides and graphitic carbon nitrides can be used as a new strategy to design high-efficiency solar water splitting photocatalysts.
we demonstrate that the combination of VS2 and g-C3N4 is a highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen production system.
the VS2/g C 3 N 4 composite is a highly efficient photocatalyst for solar driven water splitting.
